I have farmed these 5 mu in Quzhou County for 50 years. I am 68 now, and I know every piece of this land. My household has seven people. Some of my sons and daughters work in factories in the city, but they come back during sowing and harvest to help. I have a well, so I can irrigate when the weather turns dry, though I watch the electricity cost carefully.

I will plant wheat and maize in rotation on all 5 mu, just like I always have. This system feeds my family and brings in cash. For the winter wheat, I will rotary till the field before sowing in October. I will use an improved wheat variety — I buy the seeds from the shop in town. I will put down compound fertilizer as basal and topdress with urea. In total, that is about 18 kg of nitrogen, 11 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate four times: once before winter to help the seedlings, once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at heading. I will spray pesticides three times — herbicide once, and insecticide or fungicide twice if the bugs or disease show up. If the weather is normal, I expect about 500 kg per mu.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize right away. I will use no-tillage — there is no time to plough, and everyone around here plants directly into the wheat stubble to save labor and fuel. I will apply about 12 kg of nitrogen, 4 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice if it does not rain at the critical stages. I will spray pesticides three times. I expect about 550 kg per mu from the maize.

I manage it this way because it is what works. I do not experiment with new methods at my age. I use enough inputs to get a good yield, but I do not waste money. My children send money home, but the farm still needs to pay for itself.
